items.title: 67460_Sammy Price oral history interview
items.q: I think we saw Lovey Taylor... But then I met W. C. Handy on the TOBA... It was a very interesting training ground... if they were anybody, from Georgie Williams and Bessie Brown to Bert Williams to Ma Rainey to Trixie Smith...

ctx.x: No. The surprising...well....... maybe not is that it's right near Columbia University and the audiences are, I guess, mostly made up of college kids and they seem to like it.

Somebody asked me, though, over at the West End the other night, asked me to tell him the ten best records, you know, that I've made during my career. And I told him that I like "I'm Coming, Virginia" by Henry Red Allen...I place that number one, and number two was "Back Home" with Sidney Bechet, and number three was "Up Above My Head" with Rosetta Tharpe and "I Cover the Waterfront" with Doc Cheatham. And then "The Freight Train Blues" with Trixie Smith and Sidney Bechet. And then I wrote a tune back in fifties,…
Then I recorded Ida Cox's "Death Letter Blues," and then with Rosetta and Marie I made "Precious Memories." And then the next best thing that I thought I like was Doc Cheatham
